editorial:
Imagine being the new kid in town and instantly becoming the target for every mean girl in school. That is exactly what happens to Megan, a shy girl who just wants to fit in after moving with her mom. The vibe is classic nineties teen drama mixed with something much darker. When Megan finds a strange mirror, she discovers she can talk to it, and suddenly her bullies start having freak accidents. It feels like a dark fairy tale where the quiet kid finally gets some payback, but the cost is way higher than she ever expected.

You will love the slow build-up of tension and the way the mirror seems to have a mind of its own. The acting is solid for a low-budget horror flick, and the twists keep you guessing if Megan is actually crazy or if there is a real demon involved. It is not the scariest movie ever made, but it is a great popcorn watch for a Friday night.
endingExplained: In the end, you find out the mirror is not just a tool, but a portal for a wicked entity. Megan realizes the mirror has been manipulating her anger to feed on the souls of her enemies. After a final scary showdown, Megan tries to destroy the glass to stop the killing. However, the twist is that the evil presence cannot be easily erased, leaving you wondering if the cycle of horror will just start all over again.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 90s supernatural thrillers and revenge stories.
